head: 143642b
concerns: Scanner count_v2_write_authority (scan_normal_path_dependencies.py L71-90) is a crude STRING-PRESENCE check: it returns 0 if 'index_legacy_db_into_m6' and 'm6_production_indexing' appear in runner.py. Correct here (I independently read runner.py L1100-1136 and confirmed the real call), but the scanner itself is weak evidence and could pass on dead/gated code.

v2 finalize_world is STILL authoritative ALONGSIDE M6: runner.py L946-991 still runs v2 finalize, and when _v2_write_authority_on() is True, v2 finalize failure raises IndexIntegrityError (L972-978, L987-989). M6 indexing failure ALSO raises (L1132-1134). This is a DUAL-authority transition state, not a clean cutover. v2 writes still physically occur during the main loop (world_ctx in _process_unit, L906) and via finalize. 'normal_old_v2_required_writes=0' is true only in the M7.3-scoped sense (v2 is not the SOLE write authority — M6 is co-authoritative), NOT literally. M7.5 retires v2 finalize (state file honestly records normal_old_v2_finalization_dependencies=1, normal_old_v2_fallbacks=3).

M6 store metadata m6_store_status='shadow' (m6_schema.py L209-210 hardcodes 'shadow') and the m6_schema.py docstring (L3-7) still describes M6 as 'shadow tables NOT used by production queries until shadow differential testing proves QUERY_PARITY_FAILURES==0'. This is documentation lag — M7.2 already promoted M6 to production read authority (m6_native_read=32 per M7.2 gate R1). Cosmetic, not functional, but the schema's self-description contradicts the M7.2/M7.3 promotion.

No automated unit test exercises index_legacy_db_into_m6 directly (no test*m6*.py files found in repo). Materialization is proven via the corpus M6 DB (5736 facts) rather than via a regression test. Recommend adding a unit test that runs the adapter against a fixture legacy DB and asserts facts_total>0 and kind coverage.
summary: ACCEPT. M7.3 write-authority migration is GENUINE and safe for production within its stated scope. Verified against real code (not narration): (1) runner.py L1100-1136 wires index_legacy_db_into_m6 into the production indexer AFTER legacy indexing completes, gated by FW_CONTEXT_M6_WRITE_AUTHORITY (default '1'); (2) materialization is real — I independently queried the M6 store at .dsh-control/m6_research/corpus/FreeRTOS-Kernel/.fw-context/index-m6.db and found 5736 real facts (Reference 2595, ConditionalState 1009, Symbol 777, Variable 481, Call 326, Function 196, Body 154, Type 90, Field 89, EnumConstant 13, FileContent 6) with real canonical USRs (c:@F@malloc etc.); index_legacy_db_into_m6 reads from legacy tables (symbols, call_sites, refs, overrides) and writes enriched payloads to M6; (3) no silent write fallback — failure logs AND raises IndexIntegrityError (L1131-1134), never swallowed; (4) normal_old_v2_required_writes=0 (M6 is co-authoritative, v2 no longer sole authority); (5) regression intact — independently re-ran M3B scan_authority_state (PASS) and M4 scan_write_authority (machine_gate=PASS), and confirmed M7.1 (8/8 PASS) + M7.2 (10/10 PASS) result files. The 8/10 gate PASS is correct: the 2 failures (W7 fresh_verifier, W8 fresh_guardian_g6) are the PENDING fresh-review slots — this verdict fills W8. Concerns are non-blocking: v2 finalize remains co-authoritative by design (M7.5 retires it, tracked honestly in state), the v2-write scanner is string-based but its conclusion is correct here, and the M6 schema self-description still says 'shadow' (doc lag). M6-native write path is real per the §8 anti-false-migration rule: production write → M6 indexing → M6 store population, no separate extraction path.
